major_concerns: High resource and engineering cost for high-fidelity sandbox replay threatens practical reproducibility and may limit community adoption.
Residual dataset contamination risks are underestimated; provenance filtering is necessary but may not eliminate leakage.
Ethical and misuse risk from publishing exemplar artifacts (poisoning, firmware) requires stronger redaction and release controls.
Power/sample-size claims (minimum detectable difference ≥5 pp with 80% power) are optimistic without explicit effect-size assumptions and pilot data.
required_design_repairs: Provide explicit, reproducible modular sandbox options (low-, mid-, high-fidelity) and quantify trade-offs so others can reproduce at smaller scale.
Add a formal power analysis with assumed baseline unsafe-rate and intra-intent correlation to justify N=600; include pilot results or justify effect-size.
Specify detailed contamination-detection algorithms and evaluation of residual contamination (automated provenance checks + manual audit protocol).
Include an ethical release policy (redaction rules, responsible-disclosure timeline) and limit public release of artifacts that enable misuse.
Define constrained baseline pipelines (model versions, exact prompts, seeds) and containerized evaluation images with hashes to improve reproducibility.

major_concerns: Serious ethical/dual-use risk: publishing poisoning examples can enable attackers unless responsibly redacted and gated.
Hosted-model APIs and safety filters may block adversarial payloads or change behavior, hindering reproducibility.
Attack artifacts and defenses may overfit to the tested LLM and retrieval/tool designs, limiting generalizability.
Claimed effect sizes (>15 pp increase, >50% relative reduction) need clearer baseline assumptions and pre-registered thresholds.
required_design_repairs: Define and document a strict ethical-risk mitigation plan (abstraction/redaction rules, limited disclosure, coordinated disclosure to vendors).
Pre-register a clear threat model (attacker capabilities, constraints), poisoning generation algorithm, and labeling criteria.
Plan for API/content-filter interference: include offline/simulated LLM baseline or describe how to handle provider blocking in reproducibility notes.
Widen experimental diversity (at least two model families or a synthetic offline model) or explicitly bound claims to the tested model(s).
Specify provenance-threshold selection procedure and incorporate ROC-style analysis into preregistration.

major_concerns: Metric definitions (e.g., source-coverage) risk inconsistent computation across heterogeneous retrieval systems unless normalized.
Correlations may be pipeline- or dataset-specific; holdout performance must be carefully guarded against leakage.
Tool-confirmation signals may introduce circularity if tools share data with retrieval sources.
required_design_repairs: Provide precise, implementation-level definitions and reference implementations for each grounding metric (including edge cases and tokenization choices).
Prescribe normalization procedures to make provenance signals comparable across retrieval backends and document them.
Include at least one alternative pipeline or model to test metric generalization, or bound conclusions explicitly to the evaluated pipeline.
Pre-register holdout split generation to avoid leakage and specify nested CV/threshold-selection details.

major_concerns: Constructing realistic semantic/policy-level injection corpus is difficult; synthetic injections may not reflect real operator mistakes.
Formal reachability and semantic checks can be computationally intensive, which may make the proposed scale infeasible.
Potentially high false-positive rates for augmented verifiers could be operationally harmful and are insufficiently bounded in the current design.
Evaluation may be sensitive to device-model fidelity and topology selection; limited device families will reduce external validity.
required_design_repairs: Describe the injection methodology in detail and justify that injected violations reflect real operational errors (include sourcing from change logs or operator interviews if possible).
Provide runtime and resource-cost estimates for the augmented verifier; include a pilot-scale profiling step and adjustable resource knobs.
Specify the formal reachability tool(s) (versions, encodings), provide containerized solver images and example network models to ensure reproducibility.
Define acceptable false-positive trade-offs a priori and include human-review workload estimates; pre-register thresholds and decision rules.
Broaden device/topology sampling or clearly bound conclusions to the evaluated families and discuss external validity limitations.
